 City launches ‘Paso Prepared’ campaign ahead of El Niño rainy season 
Posted: 6:14 am, October 22, 2026 by News Staff 
 Council hears update on countywide storm task force, free sand sites and city maintenance work
 – Paso Robles has started a public education campaign called Paso Prepared to help residents get ready for predicted El Niño conditions. County and city emergency leaders presented an update at the Oct. 20 City Council meeting, and video of the meeting is available on the city’s YouTube channel.
 Scott Jalbert, director of the San Luis Obispo County Office of Emergency Services, described a countywide storm task force that follows the four phases of emergency management: mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery. It brings together city and county staff, public works, emergency managers, first responders and state agencies to share information and resources. The task force is using ReadySLO.org as the countywide preparedness and alert hub.
 Fire Chief Jonathan Stornetta outlined the city’s seasonal work. Goats grazed 83.36 acres in the Salinas Riverbed and 7.96 acres in Fern Canyon, mainly to reduce wildfire fuels and also to help with flood prevention. Crews also remove or chip downed trees and debris that could block stormwater flow.
 Before the rainy season, public works crews typically spend two to three weeks clearing vegetation and debris from culverts and drainage channels. This year, they cleared 16.88 tons of material from 69 drain inlets.
 City management staff also completed an Emergency Operations Center tabletop exercise to review scenarios and clarify roles. As designated disaster service workers, all city employees are trained in the FEMA Incident Command System.
 Both Stornetta and Jalbert urged residents to sign up for countywide alerts. The county runs AlertSLO and a reverse 911 system for urgent notices such as evacuation orders, and officials encourage residents to sign up for both at alertslo.org .
 The city also expanded free sand for sandbags to two self-serve locations, Pioneer Park and Sherwood Park. Residents must buy their own empty sandbags, bring a shovel and be able to fill and move the bags. Details are at prcity.com/sandbags .
 The city will host a Coffee with the City event on stormwater management and flood mitigation Oct. 30 at 7:30 a.m. at Cal Coast Beer Company. No registration is required.
 Paso Prepared will continue through the El Niño season with preparedness tips and emergency guidance on the city’s social media channels. For earlier coverage, see CHP urges residents to prepare for El Niño .
